passage: Okay, you asked, so here it is. I'm Kishore, sixteen, and the reason I skipped cricket all month is my sister Gurleen. She paid my coaching fees from her first stipend and told Mummy not to say a word. Every time I open my physics notes I think, that is her money. I said thank you once, quickly, at the door, and she waved it away. After that we only talked about dinner. I'm grateful, I really am, but it sat on my chest like a heavy bag. So yesterday I texted her: "Didi, my mock test marks went up because of you, and I know what it cost." She rang me straight away, laughing and crying a bit. Anyway, I'm going to study properly, and one day I'll treat her to chai.

qa.q: What did Gurleen pay for from her first stipend?
qa.a: She paid for Kishore's coaching fees from her first stipend.

qa.q: How does Kishore feel about the coaching money?
qa.a: Grateful yet weighed down. Kishore says it sat like a heavy bag on the chest, and thinks "that is her money" each time the physics notes come out.

qa.q: What did Kishore do that kept the debt from turning into silence?
qa.a: Kishore put the thanks in a text, saying "I know what it cost", and planned to study properly and treat her to chai.

qa.q: How might Gurleen have felt when she got the text?
qa.a: Moved and relieved to be noticed. Ringing Kishore straight away, laughing and crying a bit, suggests it meant more than the quick thank you at the door. ❤️

grounding: Kishore is thankful yet pressured after Kishore's sister paid for coaching, and puts the thanks into words instead of silence.

passage:
The mock test results were pinned on the coaching centre notice board. Shalini found her name: rank 212 out of 900, up from 480.
Her first thought was Pooja didi. Didi had paid the fees for this whole year from her first salary at the bank, without being asked. Every time Shalini opened a textbook she felt grateful, and also the weight of it. What if she didn't get in? What if all that money just vanished?
She'd been avoiding didi's calls. Talking about it felt like being checked on.
In the corridor she took out her phone. It rang twice.
"Didi? Rank 212. I wanted you to know first. And thank you, properly. I don't say it because I'm scared of letting you down."
Pooja was quiet, then laughed shakily. "Silly. I paid so you could try, not so you'd owe me."
That evening Shalini made didi's favourite poha, and they ate it on the steps.

qa.q: What rank did Shalini get in the mock test?
Why had Shalini been avoiding Pooja didi's calls?
qa.a: She felt thankful but pressured, scared of letting her sister down, so talking felt like being checked on.

qa.q: What small steps did Shalini take to thank her sister?
qa.a: She called Pooja first with the result, thanked her in words, admitted her fear, and made her favourite poha.

qa.q: How does Pooja see the fees she paid?
qa.a: Pooja sees them as a gift so Shalini can try, not as a debt, and she seems moved when Shalini finally thanks her.

grounding: A teen whose elder sister paid her coaching fees feels thankful yet pressured and thanks her in words and actions.

passage:
Dear Kiran Anna,
You're back at the hostel and I'm finally writing what I should have said at the station.
Last month when Amma found the dent in the scooter, you said you did it. You didn't. I did, practising in the lane without permission. Amma cut your pocket money and you just shrugged.
I've felt thankful and awful every single day since. Every time you smile at me I feel like I owe you something I can't pay back, so I've been quiet around you, which is stupid.
I told Amma the truth last night. She was cross, then she hugged me. You'll get your money back.
And I've made you a list of every recipe you like, for when you're home in May. I'll cook them all.
Thank you, Anna. Not for lying. For caring that much.
Your sister,
Leela

qa.q: Where was Leela practising on the scooter?
How has Leela felt since Kiran took the blame?
qa.a: Leela has felt thankful yet guilty and pressured, as if owing Kiran something that can't be paid back, which made her quiet around him.

qa.q: Which choices help Leela stop the debt turning into silence?
qa.a: She told Amma the truth, thanked Kiran in words, and is planning to cook his favourite recipes.

qa.q: How might Kiran feel reading the letter?
qa.a: He may feel touched and relieved that Leela is no longer silent, and perhaps a little embarrassed about taking the blame.

grounding: A teen whose older brother covered for her feels thankful yet pressured and thanks him in words and actions.
